content.title: Millions of eye drops recalled. See affected products.
content.text: April 3, 2026Updated April 6, 2026, 8:32 a.m. ETMillions of eye drop products have been recalled over concerns they may not be sterile, according to an enforcement report from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.On March 3, eye care product distributor K.C. Pharmaceuticals issued a voluntary recall for more than three million bottles of eye drops.The eight impacted product batches were sold under various brand names and have expiration dates ranging from April to October. They were distributed to nationwide retailers like Walgreens, Kroger and CVS.The FDA categorized it as a Class II recall on March 31. Class II, the agency's second-highest recall class, indicates that using the impacted product could cause temporary adverse health consequences.USA TODAY has reached out to K.C. Pharmaceuticals.Which eye drops have been recalled?Eight types of eye drop products that were each sold to various brands and distributors are included in the recall.Many of them can be identified through their Universal Product Code or National Drug Code numbers, which are typically found near the barcode on the bottle.They can also be identified by their lot code number, which is also printed on the bottle.Here's which eye drop products are included in the recall, according to the FDA's enforcement report:Sterile Eye Drops A.C. 0.5 fl oz (15 mL)Lot code and expiration date:AC24E01, May 31Brands and distributors:Best Choice - UPC: 0-70038-47010-6QC – Quality Choice (Sterile Eye Drops Irritation Relief) - NDC: 83324-190-14Discount Drug Mart (Eye Drops A.C.) - UPC: 0-93351-01158-0GoodSense (Sterile Eye Drops) - NDC: 50804-160-01Walgreens (Eye Drops) - UPC: 3-11917-17954-4CareOne (Itchy Relief Eye Drops)Equaline - UPC: 0-41163-25114-4TopCare Health - UPC: 0-36800-03640-6Meijer - NDC: 41250-598-01H‑E‑B A.C.
